title: automat environment profile
description: An ENVIRONMENT profile: which control sets to compile, where the account lands, what behavior is permitted inside it, and what in-account baseline to deploy. Input to `automat vend` (DESIGN 7). Named 'environment' rather than 'profile' because automat has three unrelated document types that were all called profiles — this one, obligation profiles (which regime, assessed how), and classification profiles (which institutional data level) — and an evidence record naming 'profile id + content hash' was ambiguous to exactly the auditor it exists for. 'Environment' is also the idiom higher ed already uses for a resource rated to hold data at a level. Obligation and classification profiles are POLICY artifacts; the environment profile is the thing being BUILT.

title.description: Rendered into reports, tables, and the birth certificate `vend` prints. `$defs/prose` rather than a bare non-empty string because a newline in it forges a row of one — the same reason the obligation profile's title is prose and the same defect class as an unescaped control id.

review_by.description: The date by which this environment profile must be re-read against the posture it claims to deploy. REQUIRED, with no default. An environment profile names control sets, a placement, a permitted-behavior boundary, and a baseline; left alone it keeps vending the posture someone approved once, and every account it produces looks as current as the day it was written. `verify` warns once this date has passed. The field is inside the document, so it is covered by the content hash recorded in the evidence manifest and by any attestation over it — extending the date is a change no earlier attestation vouches for.

signatures.description: Optional attestations over this document's content hash (see $defs/attestation). PROVENANCE ONLY: an attestation says who stood behind this document in what capacity — typically a central IT office recording `adopted-by` on the environment profile it publishes for departments to vend against — and never that its contents are correct, applicable, or approved for a given use. Trust is an operator determination; automat ships no trust anchor, no default accepted identity, and no verification in v1.

control_sets.description: Control set ids to compile into the artifact for this vend. Compiled by union (DESIGN 9).

permitted.description:
The PERMITTED-BEHAVIOR BOUNDARY for this environment: which regions and which service namespaces principals in the account may call. Both are ALLOWLISTS, enforced by Deny SCPs (`aws:RequestedRegion` for regions, a NotAction Deny for services) that the packer emits — a catalog author cannot write that shape, by design.

THESE ONLY EVER NARROW. Each set is INTERSECTED with the corresponding allowlist the compiled control sets require, never substituted for it and never added to it. That is the union law on the other axis: union of controls, INTERSECTION of permitted behavior (DESIGN 9). An institution therefore cannot widen its own posture by editing an environment profile — it can only restrict further, which is the whole reason the fields are safe to expose here rather than only in a control set.

DISTINCT FROM `baseline.regions`, which is opt-in region ENABLEMENT via the Account Management API. One is a boundary (what a principal may call); the other is an account-level action taken at baseline time. They are deliberately separate fields because an operator can legitimately want a region enabled but not permitted, or permitted in policy while never enabled, and conflating them would make one of those inexpressible.

regions.description: Permitted regions. Intersected with the control sets' region allowlists, never widened. `minItems: 1` because an empty allowlist is not a strict policy but a DENY-ALL: it denies every call in the account, including the ones automat's own baseline makes, and it would be discovered after create and move had already succeeded (AUDIT-0's H5 — the empty set is the absorbing element of the meet). An intersection that evaluates to empty is likewise a hard error at PLAN time naming which inputs produced the emptiness, never a silently attached deny-all.

services.description: Permitted service namespaces. Intersected with the control sets' service allowlists, never widened. `minItems: 1` for the same reason as `regions`. The globally addressed services (IAM, STS, Organizations, Route 53, Support, billing, Health, and the rest) do NOT need listing here and must not be relied on being absent: they are exempted from the region Deny by the exemption data in the control artifact (`scp.region_deny_exempt_services`), which is catalog data rather than a hardcoded list precisely because getting it wrong bricks an account.

obligations.description:
The obligation profiles this environment is being built to satisfy, by id — `cmmc-l1`, `dfars-7012`, `nih-cadr-dua`. A DIFFERENT DOCUMENT TYPE from this one: an obligation profile says under what instrument a requirement applies and how it is assessed, while this document says what gets built. Referencing them here is what lets an evidence record, and later `assess`, say which reading of policy an account was vended under without an operator re-declaring it per command.

Recorded rather than resolved: automat does not decide that an obligation applies. Where an obligation profile leaves the control catalog revision open (`revision_policy: operator-determined` — the NIH controlled-access case), the determination is the operator's and is recorded here with who made it and when, so it is inside this document's content hash and inside the evidence chain.

placement.description: Where the vended account lands. New accounts always materialize under the root and are then moved (DESIGN 3, fact 4).

target_ou.description: Destination OU id. The account is moved here after creation.

create_intermediate_ous.description: Create missing OUs on the path. Bounded by the five-level OU nesting limit (DESIGN 3, fact 10).

ou_path.description: OU names to ensure beneath target_ou, outermost first. At most five levels total under the root.

email_pattern.description:
Email template; '{name}' is substituted with the account name. Each account needs a globally unique email (DESIGN 3, fact 11).

An explicit charset rather than `[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+`: the negated form admits control characters, and this value reaches `CreateAccount` and is echoed into the birth certificate, the onboarding bundle, and every error message about the vend. The braces are admitted only for the `{name}` placeholder, which a validator checks for separately — the schema can bound the alphabet but cannot say the substitution is well-formed.

role_name.description: Name of the management-assumable role created in the child. Defaults to OrganizationAccountAccessRole (DESIGN 3, fact 6).

tags.description:
Additional tags applied at creation. automat's own conventional tags (DESIGN 14) are always applied and may not be overridden here.

The `automat:` prefix is reserved in BOTH directions, which is not a naming nicety: DESIGN 10's baseline-protection SCPs read automat's own tags in `aws:ResourceTag` conditions, so a tag an operator can write at the same scope is a tag that can be forged, and a condition that reads a forgeable tag is not a condition (AUDIT-1's C1). `propertyNames` refuses the prefix here; the SCP side is asserted by the test that enumerates which keys the policies read.

baseline.description: In-child work performed after assuming into the account (DESIGN 7, step 5).

delivery_bucket.description: S3 bucket for the delivery channel. Created in-account when absent.

regions.description: Opt-in region ENABLEMENT, via the Account Management API, performed in-child at baseline time. NOT the permitted-region boundary — that is `permitted.regions`, enforced by SCP. The two are separate fields on purpose and neither implies the other: an operator can enable a region without permitting calls in it (an account that may hold data there later), or permit one in policy that was never enabled (a boundary written ahead of the account's growth). Collapsing them would make one of those inexpressible, and would also conflate a boundary a principal cannot cross with an action automat takes once.

automation_role.description: Least-privilege in-account role automat uses for future verify runs, and which baseline-protection SCPs exempt (DESIGN 10).

disable_org_access_role_after_vend.description: Whether to restrict further use of the management-assumable role once baselining completes (DESIGN 7, step 5).

attestations.description: Where procedural-control attestation stubs are written.

evidence.description: Where evidence manifests are stored. A local copy is always written (DESIGN 11).

ou_name.description: An organizational-unit name automat will ensure exists. Bounded to the characters AWS documents for an OU name, minus the ones that make a name unusable as a name: no control bytes, no leading or trailing space, no path separator. Not a traversal defense — nothing resolves an OU name as a path — but a value with a newline in it is rendered into the plan `vend` prints before it acts, and a plan whose lines can be forged is not a plan an operator can approve.

local_dir.description:
A directory on the operator's own machine, relative to the working directory. RELATIVE AND CONTAINED: no absolute path, no `..` segment, no leading `~`. The environment profile is a file an operator may have received from a central IT office or forked from an example, so it is attacker-controlled input in the threat model, and this is the one field in it naming somewhere automat WRITES. An absolute path here would let a profile choose the destination of every attestation stub and evidence manifest a vend produces.

The `..` refusal is a separate `not` rather than a lookahead inside `pattern` because Go's regexp engine has no lookahead, and a bound the Go layer cannot state is a bound this schema must not state either — the two layers are required to agree (CLAUDE.md rule 8).

tag_key.description: An operator-supplied tag key. The `automat:` prefix is refused because automat's own conventional tags (DESIGN 14) are read by baseline-protection SCP conditions, and a key an operator can write at the same scope is one that can be forged. A separate `not` for the same reason `local_dir` gives.

tag_value.description: An operator-supplied tag value, bounded to the characters AWS permits in one. Control bytes are refused for the reason `prose` gives: tag values are rendered into the birth certificate and into `list` output.

obligation_reference.description:
One obligation profile this environment is built to satisfy, plus any determination the profile left to the operator.

The hash is required for the same reason the evidence record's is: an obligation profile is a reading of policy that moves — notices are superseded, phase-in dates arrive, a class deviation pinning a revision expires — so a reference naming only an id is a reference whose subject can be rewritten under it. A validator recomputes it; the schema cannot.

revision_determination.description: REQUIRED when the referenced obligation profile declares `revision_policy: operator-determined`, and meaningless otherwise. The schema cannot enforce that pairing — it would have to read the other document — so a validator must, and the failure is a hard error rather than a default: automat ships no default revision, because a tool that silently picks one has made a compliance determination on the institution's behalf. The whole point of recording it here is that it is then inside this document's content hash and inside the evidence chain.

operator_determination.description:
A decision automat is NOT entitled to make, recorded with who made it and when.

Every field is required, and the reason is the same for all of them: a determination with no named determiner is an anonymous claim in a document an institution acts on, and a determination with no date cannot be checked for staleness against `review_by`. The `statement` is required for the reason `attestation.statement` is — a bare value invites the reader to supply the justification themselves, and they supply the strongest one available.

Hashed with the rest of the document, so a determination cannot be rewritten under material that still verifies.

value.description: The determination itself, e.g. a control catalog revision id where the instrument names none.

determined_by.description: Who determined it, as they wish to be identified — a named person, an office, a role. Free prose because the useful identity is an institutional one, and because the point is that a human is named at all.

statement.description: The basis for the determination, in the determiner's own words.

prose.description: Single-line human text. Control characters are rejected because these strings are rendered into reports and tables, where a newline forges a row.

long_prose.description: Multi-line human text. Newlines and tabs are permitted; other control characters are not.

attestation.description: One attestation over this document's content hash: an identity, the CAPACITY it acted in, and the statement it makes. A SIGNATURE ATTESTS PROVENANCE ONLY. It never attests that the document is correct, that it applies to any particular institution, or that anyone approves of its use. The roles exist precisely so that 'X wrote this', 'Y adopted it for its own use', 'Z reviewed it' and 'the format validated' cannot collapse into a single checkmark — a reader who sees one green tick learns nothing, and would reasonably infer the strongest of the four. Whether any identity here is TRUSTED is an operator determination, made against a trust policy the operator maintains naming accepted identities per role. automat ships NO trust anchor and no default accepted identity, performs no verification in v1, and is not and must never become a registry or a standards owner.

role.description: The capacity the identity acted in, and the only thing an attestation asserts. `authored-by` — this identity wrote the document. `adopted-by` — this identity uses it, which says nothing about who wrote it. `reviewed-by` — this identity read it and stands behind having read it, not behind the contents. `interpreted-by` — this identity produced the document as its own reading of someone else's published policy, and the source institution has neither reviewed nor endorsed it. `format-validated-by` — this identity checked that the document satisfies the published schema, which is a statement about syntax and nothing else. No role means 'approved', 'certified', or 'compliant', and none may be added that does: the value of the vocabulary is that the weakest claim cannot be read as the strongest.

identity.description: Who attests, as they wish to be identified — an institution, an office, an email address, an OIDC subject. Free prose because the useful identity is an institutional one and the eventual mechanism binds it to an OIDC identity rather than to a name automat could constrain.

statement.description: REQUIRED, and the reason this is an attestation rather than a signature. The identity says in its own words what it is claiming, so a reader evaluates a sentence rather than a tick. A bare signature invites the reader to supply the claim themselves, and they supply the strongest one available. Hashed with the rest of the document, so a statement cannot be rewritten under material that still verifies.

content_sha256.description: The document content hash this attestation is over. Recorded inside the document, which the schema cannot check for self-consistency — a validator must recompute it. Present anyway, because an attestation whose subject is implicit is one that can be moved to a different document.

attested_at.description: When the attestation was made. Required for the same reason `citations[].effective_date` is: an undated claim cannot be checked for staleness, and this one ages against `review_by`.

signature.description: The cryptographic material, WHEN THERE IS ANY. Optional and deliberately subordinate to the fields above: the claim is the attestation and the bytes are evidence for it, never the other way round. An entry with no signature is still a recordable attestation — an institution asserting authorship of a file it publishes itself — while bytes with no role and no statement are not expressible at all. automat performs NO verification in v1: it does not load a trust policy, does not resolve a key, and does not treat the presence of this block as meaning anything.

format.description: `detached-ed25519` is a raw detached signature over `content_sha256`, verified against a public key the operator obtains out of band. `oidc-identity-bundle` is the intended v2 mechanism: a keyless signature bound to an OIDC identity, so an institution never has to run a key ceremony, distributed alongside the document over git or an OCI registry. Both are named now so that adopting the second is not a schema version event.

value.description: Base64-encoded signature bytes, or the base64 bundle for the keyless form.

key_id.description: Which key signed, for the detached form. Required there: a detached signature nobody can locate a key for is unverifiable, which is worse than absent because it looks verifiable.

identity_issuer.description: The OIDC issuer that authenticated `identity`, for the keyless form. Required there and FORBIDDEN on the detached form, because in the keyless model the issuer is the whole of what makes the identity mean anything: 'signed by security@example.edu' is a different claim depending on who vouched for that address.
